clusters.name: Trichotillomania (DSM p.281)
items: Recurrent pulling out of one's hair resulting in hair loss
Repeated attempts to decrease or stop hair pulling
Clinical distress or impairment in social, occupational, or academic functioning
Not attributable to another medical condition (e.g., dermatological)
Not better explained by symptoms of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD)

clusters.name: Excoriation Disorder (DSM p.284)
items: Recurrent skin picking resulting in skin lesions
Repeated attempts to decrease or stop skin picking
Clinical distress or impairment in social, occupational, or academic functioning
Not attributable to a substance (e.g., cocaine) or medical condition (e.g., scabies)
Not better explained by BDD, psychosis, stereotypic movement disorder, or NSSI

criteria.thresholds: Recurrent behavior + repeated attempts to stop + clinical distress/impairment (DSM p.281, p.284)

epidemiology.prevalence: 1-2% adults/adolescents for Trichotillomania (DSM p.282); 2.1% current / 3.1% lifetime for Excoriation (DSM p.285)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: 10:1 F:M in clinical adults, 1:1 in prepubertal children for Trichotillomania (DSM p.283); >=75% F for Excoriation (DSM p.285)
epidemiology.heritability: Increased rate in 1st-degree relatives of OCD and BFRB probands (DSM p.283, p.286)
comorbidities: OCD and Anxiety Disorders (DSM p.284, p.287)
epidemiology.prognosis: Chronic waxing and waning course without treatment (DSM p.283, p.285)

etiology.genetic: Familial aggregation with OCD and OCRDs (DSM p.283, p.286)
etiology.neurobiology: Ventral CSTC loop (Accumbens-VMPFC) impulsivity migrating to Dorsal CSTC loop (Striatum-OFC) habit circuit; striatal glutamatergic hyperactivity (StahlNeuro p.539-540, p.576; Dulcan p.190, p.369)
etiology.environmental: Triggered by stress, anxiety, boredom, or dermatological conditions like acne excoriée (DSM p.285; Dulcan p.445)

first_line: CBT Habit Reversal Training (HRT) / CBIT (Awareness training, competing response 1-2 min, stimulus control) (Dulcan p.431, p.449)
second_line: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) 1,200-2,400 mg/day (Dulcan p.190, p.227; StahlNeuro p.576)
SSRIs for comorbid anxiety/depression (Fluoxetine, Sertraline, Fluvoxamine) (StahlNeuro p.576; StahlKids p.199, p.229, p.439)
Augmentation: Aripiprazole, Risperidone, Naltrexone (Dulcan p.122, p.381; StahlNeuro p.571; StahlKids p.37)
key_side_effects: Clomipramine: QTc prolongation, arrhythmias, anticholinergic effects, sedation (Dulcan p.332; StahlKids p.125-127)
NAC: Mild GI distress (Dulcan p.190, p.227)
SSRIs: Suicidal ideation black box warning, activation in youth (Dulcan p.261; StahlKids p.202)
treatment.monitoring: Baseline and post-titration ECG for Clomipramine (Dulcan p.332; StahlKids p.127); GI evaluation for Trichobezoar/Rapunzel syndrome if trichophagia present (DSM p.283; Dulcan p.417)

items: CY-BOCS - Children's Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Dulcan p.374, p.445)
MGH-HPS - Massachusetts General Hospital Hair Pulling Scale (Dulcan p.445)
SPS - Skin Picking Scale / NIMH Skin Picking Scale (Dulcan p.445)
COIS - Child OCD Impact Scale (Dulcan p.375)
Dermoscopy / Trichoscopy showing broken hairs of varying shaft length (DSM p.283)
key_numbers: 1-2 minutes for Competing Response holding time (Dulcan p.431)

items: Alopecia Areata / Telogen Effluvium (DSM p.283-284)
Scabies / Acne excoriée / Eczema (DSM p.286-287)
Dermatitis Artefacta / Factitious Disorder (DSM p.287)
Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) (DSM p.272-273, p.284, p.286)
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) (DSM p.264, p.284, p.286)
Stereotypic Movement Disorder (DSM p.89, p.284, p.286)
Nonsuicidal Self-Injury (NSSI) (DSM p.286, p.924)
Substance-Induced Picking (Cocaine/Amphetamines) (DSM p.287, p.289)
key_numbers: <3 years typical onset age for Stereotypic Movement Disorder vs puberty for BFRBs (DSM p.89, p.283)
10:1 adult F:M ratio helping differentiate BFRBs from non-gendered mimics (DSM p.283)

high_yield: Trichotillomania sex ratio is 1:1 in prepubertal children but 10:1 female in adults (DSM p.283).
Trichophagia can lead to Trichobezoar (Rapunzel Syndrome), causing bowel obstruction or perforation (DSM p.283; Dulcan p.417).
BFRBs lack cognitive obsessions; they are driven by sensory premonitory urges and tension/relief loops (DSM p.264).
Neurobiologically, BFRBs reflect a shift from Ventral Striatum (impulsivity) to Dorsal Striatum (habit circuit) with loss of top-down inhibition (StahlNeuro p.539-540).
Habit Reversal Training (HRT) / CBIT is the first-line evidence-based psychotherapy (Dulcan p.431, p.449).
N-acetylcysteine (NAC) 1,200-2,400 mg/day is the key evidence-supported glutamatergic agent in youth (Dulcan p.190; StahlNeuro p.576).
Clomipramine requires mandatory baseline and post-titration ECG monitoring due to QTc prolongation risk (Dulcan p.332; StahlKids p.127).
